description: ROS 2 graph only; on a DDS-only setup use `list_endpoints` or `peek_dds_samples` on `DCPSPublication` / `DCPSSubscription`. Collect up to `count` live messages from a ROS 2 `topic`, waiting at most `timeout_s` seconds, as a `SampleResult`. **Live mode** streams `ros2 topic echo` with the publishers' QoS (latched topics work) and returns what arrived by the deadline: `count` is the actual number and `note` says `N of M messages` and why it is short (no publisher, silent, slow or too large to print in time; a latched topic usually holds one message, so use `count` 1). Each sample has `payload` (nested named values), `timestamp_ns` (the publisher's clock, sim time on a simulation, 0 for a headerless message such as `std_msgs/String`; see `stamp_source`) and `received_ns` (wall clock when the CLI printed it). **Arrays**: arrays, strings and bytes are cut at 128 elements by default (a 541-beam `LaserScan` loses beams 128 and up); cut fields are listed in `payload._truncated_fields` and `note`. Raise `max_array_length` (up to 65536, or null) or set `arrays_summary_only`. A message over the 1 MiB cap (`TOPICFORGE_MAX_SAMPLE_BYTES`) is dropped with a `note`. **Mock mode** returns demo-robot samples instantly. **Raises an MCP error** without a `ros2` CLI, for an unknown topic, or when the CLI fails. Read-only; never publishes. **Summary and rate**: `LaserScan`, `Odometry`, `Imu`, `Image` and `PointCloud2` samples carry a `summary` of the whole message (other types: null); `rate` gives frequency, interval spread and a `verdict` measured on `received_ns` (when the CLI printed each message). Use `count` >= 10 (50 above 20 Hz); a multi-publisher topic such as `/tf` reads `erratic` without being broken. **Duration**: runs the `ros2` CLI behind the ROS lock, one call at a time. It returns within `timeout_s` (at most 40) plus about 3 s to stop the CLI and decode; the whole call, lock wait included, ends within 45 s: a call that cannot get the lock fails at once with a `busy` error (retry), and one that waited has less time to collect.

arrays_summary_only.description: When true, arrays become a type-and-length summary: use it to read the non-array fields of large messages. Default false.

count.description: Messages to wait for, default 5, at most 50 (more is capped and `note` says so); 0 returns nothing. Fewer arrive when the topic is slow or `timeout_s` runs out.

max_array_length.description: Longest array, string or bytes value returned in full, 1..65536, default 128 (a 541-beam `LaserScan` is cut to 128 ranges; its `summary` still covers all). Longer values are cut and listed in `_truncated_fields`. Null returns everything (large for images and clouds; a message over 1 MiB is dropped with a note).

timeout_s.description: Seconds to wait, 1..40, default 10, covering topic lookup and CLI start-up. The call returns within `timeout_s` plus a few seconds, with what arrived and a `note`. Raise it for a topic slower than 1 Hz.

topic.description: Fully qualified ROS 2 topic name starting with `/`, e.g. `/cmd_vel`. Segments are letters, digits and underscores (not starting with a digit); anything else is rejected before reaching the `ros2` CLI.

name: sample_messages

payload.description: Message fields as nested values; `nan`/`inf` are strings. Live `sample_messages` adds `_truncated_fields` (cut paths) and `_raw_text` (unparsable output).

received_ns.description: Wall-clock ns when the `ros2` CLI printed the message (live `sample_messages` only).

recorded_ns.description: Bag record time in ns (`peek_bag_samples` only).

summary.description: Condensed reading of the whole message (see `summary_type`); `null` for other types and DDS peeks.

timestamp_ns.description: Publisher-clock ns: `header.stamp`, else the time in the body of `Clock`, `TFMessage` or `Log`, else 0 (see `stamp_source`); not the arrival time.

basis.description: Clock the rate is measured on: `received_ns` (live) or `recorded_ns` (bag).

clock_basis.description: Stamp clock: `wall` (stamps are dates), `sim` (since a start), `none` (no stamps), `mixed` (several kinds, e.g. two publishers).

interval_cv.description: Interval standard deviation over mean; `null` under 2 messages.

message_count.description: Messages the rate is computed from.

observed_frequency_hz.description: Messages per second on `basis`, drain excluded; the rate the caller received. `null` under 2 messages.

sim_frequency_hz.description: Same rate on the messages' own stamps (publisher clock); `null` without advancing stamps.

stamp_age_median_s.description: Median of arrival minus stamp, s, if `wall`; negative = publisher ahead.

stamp_age_p95_s.description: 95th percentile of that age (max under 20 messages).

stamp_regression_count.description: Times a stamp went back versus the previous one.

startup_burst_count.description: Leading messages set aside as a start-up drain (live only); still in `message_count`.

trailing_gap_s.description: Time from the last message to the end of a live observation; else `null`.

verdict.description: First match: `silent` (none), `insufficient` (under 5), `intermittent` (an interval over 3x the median), `stable` (cv < 0.2), `jittery` (< 0.5), `erratic`. Describes this window, not a diagnosis.

count.description: Number of samples in `samples`: fewer than requested when the topic gave fewer, never more than 50 (a larger request is capped to 50).

note.description: Why `samples` is empty or limited, when not obvious; else `None`.

rate.description: How the topic delivered the messages, with a verdict; `null` for `peek_dds_samples`. Use `count` >= 10.

title: Sample topic messages
